faq.question: Does Apple Intelligence text generation work offline?
faq.answer: Yes. The Foundation Models framework runs Apple's on-device model, so generation works without a network connection once Apple Intelligence is enabled and its model is downloaded.

faq.question: Can I use the Foundation Models framework on iOS 18?
faq.answer: No. The framework requires iOS 26. Your Capacitor app can still support older iOS versions, because the plugin only calls Foundation Models when it is available and reports a readiness message otherwise.

faq.question: Which iPhones support Apple Intelligence for developers?
faq.answer: iPhone 15 Pro and 15 Pro Max, and iPhone 16 models and later, running iOS 26 with Apple Intelligence turned on. iPads with M1 or later and iPad mini with A17 Pro also qualify.

faq.question: Does using Apple Intelligence cost anything?
faq.answer: No. The on-device model is free to use, with no API key and no per-token billing. @capgo/capacitor-llm is open source as well.

faq.question: Does the same code work on Android?
faq.answer: Yes. With @capgo/capacitor-llm you switch the model path to 'Gemini Nano' on supported Android phones, or load a Gemma model, and keep the same chat and event code.

This guide covers what the framework offers, device requirements, a complete TypeScript integration, the 4,096-token context window, error handling, App Review notes, and how the same code runs on Android.
What Apple Intelligence offers app developers
With iOS 26, Apple opened its on-device foundation model to third-party apps through the
framework. In Swift you work with
. The plugin wraps those so your web code can use them:

The model is roughly 3 billion parameters. It is good at summarizing, rewriting, extracting, classifying, and short-form generation. It is not a replacement for a large cloud model on open-ended knowledge questions, and Apple says as much in its own guidance. Design features around text the user already has.

The on-device model has a context window of 4,096 tokens. Everything counts toward it: instructions, every previous turn in the chat, the new prompt, and the response being generated. When a session exceeds it, Foundation Models throws an "exceeded context window size" error, which reaches you as a
One chat per task, not one chat per screen.

Prompts and responses stay on the device, so on-device generation adds no data collection to your privacy label by itself. Two things are still on you:
Apple publishes acceptable use requirements for the Foundation Models framework. Read them before you ship, especially for features that generate content shown to other users.
The model has built-in guardrails and may refuse some prompts or outputs. Treat a refusal as a normal result and show a clear message.

Apple Intelligence brings a free, private, offline language model to every eligible iPhone on iOS 26, and a Capacitor app can use it with a few lines of TypeScript. Select the model, gate the UI on
, keep each task in its own short chat, stream snapshots into the UI, and handle refusals and context errors as normal outcomes. For a broader take on shipping AI features in hybrid apps, read
